discovery: Photonic crystals: photonic band gaps and the control of spontaneous emission and light localization in periodic dielectric structures
motivation: In 1987, Eli Yablonovitch and Sajeev John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can have a complete photonic band gap, a range of frequencies in which light cannot propagate. Yablonovitch showed that such a gap suppresses spontaneous emission. John showed that disorder can localize light strongly. Yablonovitch then fabricated the first three-dimensional photonic band-gap crystal ('Yablonovite'), which turned the idea into a working material. Photonic crystals showed that the electromagnetic vacuum itself can be engineered. This idea underlies modern nanophotonics: ultrahigh-Q nanocavities, slow light, photonic-crystal fibres, low-threshold nanolasers, and solid-state cavity quantum electrodynamics, in which single quantum dots and colour centres are strongly coupled to light on a chip. Photonic crystals are now a standard tool in quantum optics, telecommunications and integrated photonics, used in thousands of laboratories and in industry. This conceptual advance in physics merits the Nobel Prize.
